<algorithm>\n#include <array>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n#ifndef M_PI\n#define M_PI 3.14159265358979323846\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT_2\n#define M_SQRT_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_SQRT1_2\n#define M_SQRT1_2 0.7071067811865475244\n#endif\n#ifndef M_1_SQRTPI\n#define M_1_SQRTPI 0.564189583547756286948\n#endif\n\nenum OptionType {\n    CALL = 0,\n    PUT = 1\n};\n\nstruct OptionInput {\n    int type;           // CALL or PUT\n    double strike;      // Strike price\n    double spot;        // Spot price\n    double q;           // Dividend yield\n    double r;           // Risk-free rate\n    double t;           // Time to maturity\n    double vol;         // Volatility\n    double value;       // Expected value (for validation)\n    double tol;         // Tolerance\n};\n\n// Standard normal cumulative distribution function\ninline double cumulativeNormal(const double x) noexcept {\n    return 0.5 * (1.0 + std::erf(x * M_SQRT1_2));\n}\n\n// Standard normal probability density function\ninline double normalPDF(const double x) noexcept {\n    return M_1_SQRTPI * M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\ndouble blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = option.spot;\n    const double K = option.strike;\n    const double r = option.r;\n    const double q = option.q;\n    const double T = option.t;\n    const double sigma = option.vol;\n    \n    if (T <= 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n    \n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n    \n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n    \n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S * exp(-q * T) * Nd1 - K * discount * Nd2;\n    } else { // PUT\n        price = K * discount * cumulativeNormal(-d2) - S * exp(-q * T) * cumulativeNormal(-d1);\n    }\n    \n    return price;\n}\n\n// Standard test cases for validation\ninline constexpr std::array<OptionInput, 7> getTestOptions() noexcept {\n    return {{\n        {CALL, 40.00, 42.00, 0.04, 0.08, 0.75, 0.35, 5.0975, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0205, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {CALL, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9413, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 90.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 9.9210, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 100.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 1.8734, 1.0e-3},\n        {PUT, 100.00, 110.00, 0.10, 0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.0408, 1.0e-3},\n    }};\n}\n\n// Generate a larger set of options by scaling the test set\nvoid generateOptions(std::vector<OptionInput>& options, const size_t numOptions) {\n    constexpr auto testOptions = getTestOptions();\n    options.resize(numOptions);\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numOptions; ++i) {\n        // Cycle through test options and vary parameters slightly\n        const OptionInput& base = testOptions[i % testOptions.size()];\n        options[i] = base;\n        \n        // Add some variation for larger datasets\n        const double factor = 1.0 + 0.1 * (i / static_cast<double>(testOptions.size()));\n        options[i].spot *= factor;\n        options[i].strike *= factor;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResults(const std::vector<OptionInput>& options, \n                     const std::vector<double>& results) {\n    bool allPassed = true;\n    const int numChecks = std::min(static_cast<size_t>(10), options.size());\n    \n    printf(\"Checking computed option prices:\\n\");\n    for (int i = 0; i < numChecks; ++i) {\n        const double computed = results[i];\n        const double expected = options[i].value;\n        const double error = fabs(computed - expected);\n        const double relError = error / (fabs(expected) + 1e-10);\n        \n        printf(\"  Option %d: computed=%.4f, expected=%.4f, rel_error=%.4e\\n\", \n               i, computed, expected, relError);\n        \n        // Relaxed validation - just check values are positive and reasonable\n        if (computed < 0.0 || computed > 1000.0 || std::isnan(computed) || std::isinf(computed)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed at option %d: invalid value %.4f\\n\", i, computed);\n            allPassed = false;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return allPassed;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Number of options to price (default: 10000)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation against known values\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t numOptions = 10000;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            numOptions = atoll(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Black-Scholes Option Pricing Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Number of options: %zu\\n\", numOptions);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? results(numOptions);\n    \n    // Price options\n    printf(\"Pricing options...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < numOptions; ++i) {\n        results[i] = blackScholes(options[i]);\n    }\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::microseconds>(end {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1NPjQ55w3r32XSF3JYm","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Black-Scholes benchmark now prices options on the GPU, and the build is unconditionally CUDA. It runs about 16× faster than the original at 10⁸ options, but its output is not bit-identical to the CPU version.\n\n**Changes (only the two existing files):**\n- `black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp`: one thread per option with a grid-stride loop, 256-thread blocks. Option inputs are generated on the device from the index, so the only transfer is the results back to the host. The 7-entry test table sits in `__constant__` memory. `blackScholes` and its helpers are `__host__ __device__`. Validation takes the expected values from the test table instead of a host-side options array.\n- `black-scholes/CMakeLists.txt`: enables CUDA as a required language, compiles the existing `.cpp` as CUDA, and targets the GPU present at configure time (`CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native`). The host `-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra` flags are forwarded through nvcc. The minimum CMake version rises to 3.24, which `native` requires.\n\n**Choices I made:**\n- I kept `.cpp` rather than adding a `.cu` file, since you asked for no new files.\n- The timed region covers the kernel and the device-to-host copy. CUDA context creation and device allocation happen before the timer, as the original's vector allocation did.\n- The executable name, CLI flags, output format and validation logic are unchanged.\n\n**Verification:**\n- Builds with no warnings on CUDA 12.0, RTX 3090 (sm_86).\n- `-v` passes at 10k and 1M options. Usage and unknown-option handling match the original; `-n 0` and `-n 1` run cleanly.\n- Output is not bit-identical. At 10k options the Sum agrees to ~1e-16 relative, while the deep-tail sample `Sample[2500]` differs by ~2.6e-12 relative, so the hash differs. Disabling FMA contraction does not fix it, which points to device `erf`/`exp`/`log` versus glibc. I could not match those bit-for-bit on the GPU, and I left the formula unchanged so semantics stay the same.\n\n**Performance** (single run for the original, three runs for CUDA):\n\n| Options | CPU original | CUDA |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1M | ~90 ms | ~6 ms |\n| 10M | ~898 ms | ~57 ms |\n| 100M | ~9.1 s | ~0.55 s |\n\nThe ceiling is FP64 throughput: this GeForce part runs double precision at a fraction of its FP32 rate, and I kept double to preserve results.\n\n**Not done:** multi-GPU distribution and pinned host memory for the result copy. Both are possible follow-ups if you want more throughput at very large sizes.\n\nI built out-of-tree in `/tmp`, so the repo contains only the two edited files. `output.txt` and `common/` are untouched."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1005,"cache_read_input_tokens":46411,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1005},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"abdd99b8-e8df-4be8-95e3-3e8b88f68f54","uuid":"8dbfa507-7ec6-465d-8be9-03982233337f","timestamp":"2026-10-14T02:50:31.238Z","request_id":"req_011Cg1NPj7xYFBETMSSREpk4"}
